title: Cowboys OC Klayton Adams on wanting the team to get a hot dog fridge: “It’s something I’m working on here. How can you really have a break room or a snack room if you don’t have a hot dog fridge? And if you’re gonna have a hot dog fridge, you have to have high quality hot dogs in it. And if you’re gonna have high quality hot dogs, we have to have brioche buns and maybe some pretzel buns. “These are all things that we’re working on. Maybe an industrial-sized 7-Eleven hot dog roller. I don’t know. These are just things that roll around in the back of my mind. “One of the things I learned from going to Disneyland with my kids, because I was trying to steam the bun, I was trying to toast the bun, and the guy at Disneyland goes, ‘No, man, put it in the bun and then wrap it in foil and let the hot dog steam the bun.’ It’s been revolutionary.”

title: Eagles Training Camp Player Of The Day, Day 13/Day 1 vs NE: Will Shipley got some unexpectedly great opportunities on Wednesday vs. the Patriots and he made the most of them Shipley looked awesome running the ball as he got the majority of the RB2 carries with the first-team offense. Part of the reason Shipley got those carries is likely because Tank Bigsby is dealing with a toe injury, but whatever the reason, Shipley helped his stock. Shipley’s best play of the day was a reception from Jalen Hurts on a wheel route. Hurts had pressure in his face but made the right read (on what seemed like a good play call) and found Shipley streaking down the right sideline for what was probably a 60ish yard gain. Shipley had good speed on the play but he was just caught from behind before breaking free for the final few yards for the touchdown. Shipley came into camp probably needing to earn a roster spot and not locked into a role. Wednesday’s practice might have been enough to ensure he will be on the team.

title: I just personally think it's impossible to determine who won a practice. There are 11-on-11s between top units happening simultaneously on separate fields. I watched the Patriots' defense today. They got gashed by the run but also brought more pressure than I expected. Outside of 7-on-7s, when I was primarily watching DL/OL 1-on-1s, the Patriots' coverage wasn't exceptional. So, who won? I can't say, because I was only locked in on the Patriots' offense for the final two-minute drills. But the Eagles are supposed to be a good team, and at the very least, the Patriots were competitive against them. It was absolutely not the shit show that we saw in 2024 joint practices.

title: Jalen Hurts Training Camp Stats, Day 13/Day 1 vs. Pats: Wednesday’s practice was a great example of why all stats need context. The numbers for the day were not good — 3 interceptions is most Jalen Hurts has ever thrown in a training camp practice. There were some positive moments and some context to the interceptions. Hurts had two really nice throws on the day which resulted in big gains. The first was a deep pass to Elijah Moore which was nearly a 45+ yard touchdown but Moore was down just short of the end zone. The throw was perfect and right in stride for Moore, who threw the ball up in the air celebrating after the big play. The second was a wheel route(ish) completion to Will Shipley on what seemed to be a blitz. Hurts moved back in the pocket, allowing Shipley to get down the field before lofting it to Shipley about 15ish yards in the air. The throw gave Shipley plenty of room to run and he got about 30ish more yards after the catch. The was a mixture of blame on the interceptions. The first was a pass that Hurts threw right to Wicks but it bounced off his hands and the Patriots defender got to it before it hit the ground. The second was a short, quick pass to Covey but there must have been a miscommunication as the ball went right to a Patriots defender, who ran it back for a pick-six. The third interception was on Hurts it seemed. The pass was it seemed on a crossing route over the middle of the field but it sailed on Hurts and was picked off. Hurts also failed to lead the offense on a scoring drive in the final drill of the day after Drake Maye lead the Patriots offense to a field goal. Overall Hurts didn’t have as bad of a day as the stats indicate. He was playing without Devonta Smith for all of the team drills. Still, 3 turnovers, no touchdowns and no points in the final drive is not a good day for Hurts or the Eagles offense. Day 13 Stats: 19/27, 0 TD, 3 INT 2026 Stats: 157/226, 10 TD, 9 INT

title: Eagles vs Patriots: Day 1 Win/Loss Verdict Day 1 was everything joint practices are supposed to be — intense practice with lots of competitive reps What was surprising was how the Eagles defense/secondary struggled Obviously all of these things are true: There is no hitting the QB, no game planning, etc etc. But it was a bit shocking how well the Patriots passed the ball against the Eagles. AJ Brown had 6 catches including three over 20 yards. One was a down the sideline completion for probably 30+ yards. Romeo Doubs also had a good day including a deep pass down the left sideline over Woolen, who had a rough day. Overall Drake Maye was 21/25, a sign of just how much success he had vs the Eagles defense On offense the most encouraging part was the Eagles ran the ball really well. They created some huge holes and in a real game likely had some big gains. Considering how much the running game struggled last season it was a big positive how good the running game looked vs the Patriots. The passing game wasn’t as good. They did have two big gains — one to Elijah Moore on a deep pass and one to Will Shipley on a wheel route. Outside of that, however, they didn’t get much going without Devonta Smith doing team reps. Jalen Hurts had 3 interceptions (all in 7v7), which is a very high number for him. This practice was decided at the end in the biggest reps of the day. The Patriots offense drove into Eagles territory and got a field foal. The Eagles offense had a tough time moving the ball and didn’t get a field goal. Overall this was a close practice until the end but the Patriots get the win.
